image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of the head and upper snout of a Nile crocodile resting on sandy ground. The image highlights the textured, armored skin, the eye with a vertical pupil, and the interlocking teeth along the jawline.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout tapers to a distinct point (V-shape), consistent with Crocodylus niloticus morphology, distinguishing it from the U-shaped snout of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple large, conical teeth are clearly visible protruding from the lower jaw and fitting into notches/along the upper jaw line, demonstrating the characteristic interlocking arrangement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is located on the top ridge of the skull (dorsal). The pupil is a distinct vertical slit. A translucent film (nictitating membrane) appears to be partially covering or protecting the eye, which is biologically accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The extreme tip of the snout where the nostrils are located is cut off by the right edge of the image frame; therefore, this feature cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible neck and shoulder region show thick, rugged skin indicative of heavy armor, consistent with an elongated reptilian body structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture displays distinct, raised, bony plates (scutes) that appear to follow a linear, longitudinal pattern along the back of the neck/head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of earthy browns, greens, and greys. The texture is visibly rough, cracked, and granular, matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image angle is dorsal/lateral; the belly (ventral surface) is completely occluded by the ground and the animal's own body mass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of the head; no limbs or feet are visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the field of view.
